transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (CSM), Diego (SE), Aisha (Novarise), Tom (CTO), Priya (Platform), Ben (SRE)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): QBR check in. Discussed increased usage, spike in tail latency, cost optimization, and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR — we'll do a quick agenda rundown, usage, cost, reliability, then roadmap and next steps. Can everyone hear me ok?
00:12 Aisha: Yep loud and clear. Thanks Maya.
00:16 Tom: Good to be here.
00:20 Maya: Cool. Omar, want to kick off with the adoption highlights?
00:24 Omar: Sure — so we looked at Q1 to Q2 trends, Novarise has ramped from about 120k tokens/day to 310k tokens/day, so roughly a 2.5x increase month over month on a few endpoints, most traffic's coming from the summarization pipeline and the new in-product chat. Costs have scaled similarly, and there was a notable jump when the team enabled longer context on a subset of requests.
00:40 Priya: Yeah, that was us enabling 8k context for research prompts, we forgot to pin a model variant so some requests hit larger models.
00:50 Diego: Right, that config change explains the token growth and the latency tail — larger models and longer sequences increase KV cache pressure. We saw the p95 go from 420ms to about 1.1s on hosted during the peak.
01:05 Ben: We also had two incidents early April where a cluster autoscaler misconfigured and added a cold node which spiked latency for ~12 minutes. Not a Redwood fault per se but wanted to flag it.
01:15 Maya: Thanks Ben. On the cost side, we prepared an updated cost breakdown — quick note, our hosted pricing shows higher unit cost at odd hours due to burst capacity charges when you exceed the quota. So two levers: batching/cache tuning and, if you want predictability, Dedicated commit would smooth unit price.
01:33 Aisha: We're trying to understand the tradeoff. Dedicated seems cheaper per token but we worry about sustained throughput needs and overprovisioning. Also, what about data residency and encryption? For some logs we need KMS and customer managed keys.
01:46 Diego: Dedicated has predictable throughput and you can pin a hardware profile. For KMS/HSM and zero-eavesdrop we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) — that gives you a customer-managed control plane, SAML/SSO, and KMS integration. We can also enable audit logs and longer retention. There's a deployment checklist.
02:03 Tom: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts we can share with the security team? They kept asking for evidence.
02:09 Omar: Yes, we can share SOC 2 and ISO summaries; the C-suite pack plus the architecture diagram. We'll follow up with the full artifacts link.
02:18 Priya: On performance, Diego, can you run a bench to compare Dedicated vs Hosted at our typical mix? We want p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
02:27 Diego: Absolutely — I suggest a 1-hour benchmark with your production prompt mix plus a stress test. I'll spin up a Dedicated profile matching your throughput and run the same on hosted. We'll also measure cold-starts and KV cache warmup.
02:38 Aisha: Perfect. Also curious about quantization — can you recommend safe quantization profiles that don't regress our outputs? We care about perceived quality for customer-facing copy.
02:47 Diego: Yep, Redwood Optimize has model/quantization recommendations; we can run A/B evals on your prompt set to verify regression thresholds. We'll include that in the benchmark plan.
02:59 Maya: Quick note on rollout and reliability: we recommend canary and automatic fallback policies — if a Dedicated variant is overloaded, requests can route to Hosted compatible model. That helped another customer avoid downtime.
03:10 Ben: How does request routing affect latency and cost? If we fallback to Hosted mid-flight, will tokens be double-billed?
03:18 Diego: No double billing — fallback happens at request time, and we charge the final serving path. There is some added latency on reroute but it's usually within a few 100ms. We can show traces in the Console.
03:28 Tom: Anything on retention and logs? We need audit logs for compliance and also to tie errors back to user sessions.
03:34 Omar: Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM and we support custom retention windows. For Private installs, logs can remain in your VPC.
03:41 Aisha: Great. On license/contract: if we do Dedicated commit for 6 months, can we get a cost uplift discount?
03:47 Maya: Yes, we typically offer commit-based discounts — terms vary by size. I'll send a pricing sheet with scenarios: 3-month, 6-month, 12-month commitments and expected unit costs.
03:58 Priya: Any blockers on doing a pilot Private deployment — like network reqs?
04:03 Diego: For Private (VPC/on-prem) we need VPC peering, firewall rules, and access to your KMS endpoint if you want CMK. Some baseline infra and a maintenance window to cutover. We also provide an installer script and a runbook.
04:15 Ben: Our infra lead wants to know if there's any special NTP or certificate requirements — can you list them?
04:20 Omar: Yes, we'll provide an infra checklist in the follow-up.
04:24 Aisha: Ok next, reliability incidents — any patterns from your side?
04:28 Diego: The main pattern was from mixed model sizes and long sequences causing batching inefficiencies. Also, the autoscaler behavior Ben mentioned. We recommend prefix caching for your standard prompts plus a batching tuning pass. That usually reduces token cost ~18-25% and lowers p95.
04:43 Tom: Sounds good. Can we get a prioritized roadmap of features that'll help us — like structured output, function calls, or streaming improvements?
04:50 Maya: We'll include a short roadmap doc. Highlights: improved streaming reliability next quarter, more quantization profiles, and expanded Dedicated hardware options. We'll flag items relevant to Novarise.
04:59 Aisha: Excellent. Anything else?
05:02 Maya: Quick recap of next steps: we'll send cost breakdown, SOC2/ISO artifacts, infra checklist, and schedule the perf benchmark. Diego will run the Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark and include quantization A/B tests. Customer to decide on pilot extension timeline.
05:18 Tom: Thanks all.
05:22 Aisha: Thanks, looking forward to the benchmark.
05:25 Maya: Great — we'll follow up via email with links.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-heard words — e.g., "KV cash" appears in raw auto-transcript. References to Redwood products: Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize; sometimes spelled slightly wrong in the transcript.

End of transcript.
